h: Petrol prices fall by up to ₦85 a litre as Dangote suspends diesel price cut
p: Petrol pump prices have reportedly fallen by between ₦25 and ₦85 per litre in a week as refiners and importers compete. Dangote Refinery has, however, withdrawn a planned ₦150 cut in diesel prices pending a review.
body: Motorists are seeing some relief at filling stations, with petrol prices reportedly falling by between ₦25 and ₦85 per litre over the past seven days.

The reductions follow fresh price cuts by Dangote Refinery, importers and major marketers, amid growing competition between locally refined and imported petrol. Dangote has cut its petrol price several times this month, most recently to ₦1,070 per litre on 19 November, its lowest quoted rate since July.

However, Dangote Refinery has withdrawn an earlier announcement that it would reduce the gantry price of diesel from ₦1,720 to ₦1,570 per litre. In a new message to customers, the refinery said the proposed ₦150 cut, which was meant to take effect on Saturday, 21 November, was still under internal review.
Marketers and businesses that rely on diesel are now waiting for clarity on the new rate.

Depot prices of petrol and diesel fell between 16 and 20 November in Lagos, Warri, Port Harcourt and Calabar. Lagos saw the biggest cuts, with some depots reducing petrol by as much as ₦120 per litre.

A market survey on Saturday, 21 November, put Dangote's ex-gantry petrol price at ₦1,060 per litre, down ₦99 from ₦1,159. However, some MRS, AP and other filling stations were still selling at between ₦1,250 and ₦1,300 per litre, well above the depot price, leaving motorists waiting for the cuts to reach the pump.
more: Petrol prices have fallen by up to ₦85 a litre.
Dangote's ₦150 diesel cut is under review.
Competition with imported petrol is driving prices down.
